q: What position is used for microvascular decompression?
why: Park bench gives access to the cerebellopontine angle with the head in pins.

q: Which reflex can cause bradycardia when the trigeminal nerve is handled?
why: Stimulation of the trigeminal nerve can cause sudden bradycardia and hypotension.

q: Why put the cannula on the side of surgery?
o: It faces up once the patient is in park bench
It is easier to reach the vein
why: In park bench the operative side is uppermost, so lines stay accessible.

q: Why might fentanyl be used instead of remifentanil at induction?
o: Less hypotension while you are away positioning the patient
why: A smoother BP during positioning, when you can't easily treat hypotension, helps.

q: Which nerve is at risk in surgery near the cerebellopontine angle?
why: Hearing loss (VIII) is a recognised risk; facial nerve (VII) too.
